description: We are a team of technology enthusiasts with a strong interest in Artificial Intelligence, Software Development, Data Science, and Space Exploration. Our goal is to combine creativity, technical knowledge, and teamwork to develop innovative solutions to real-world challenges using NASA's open data.
summary:
We developed an accessible SPHEREx Sky Time-Lapse Viewer that allows users to compare infrared observations of the same sky region at two different times. The application aligns and quality-filters NASA SPHEREx images, corrects background and resolution differences, measures brightness changes, and presents the results through observation frames, an animated GIF, a change heatmap, reliability indicators, and candidate features for further investigation.

The project addresses the challenge by transforming complex SPHEREx FITS data into an interactive and understandable experience for both the public and researchers. Results can be downloaded as PDF, JSON, or GIF, while a precomputed offline version ensures a reliable presentation without depending on live archive availability.

This is important because meaningful astronomical changes can be difficult to identify across large scientific datasets. Our tool makes these comparisons more accessible while clearly distinguishing potential candidates from confirmed discoveries and explaining the limitations of the analysis.
details:
Our project is an accessible SPHEREx Sky Time-Lapse Viewer that compares NASA infrared observations of the same sky region at two different dates. It quality-filters and aligns the images, matches their wavelengths and resolution, measures brightness changes, and presents the results through frames, an animated GIF, a heatmap, reliability checks, and candidate features for further investigation.

The project makes complex astronomical data easier to explore while clearly explaining that detected changes are candidates, not confirmed discoveries. Its intended impact is to support education, public engagement, and future multi-epoch astronomical research.

We used Python, Flask, Astropy, NumPy, SciPy, Reproject, Matplotlib, Pillow, ReportLab, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Aladin Lite, NASA SPHEREx data, and NASA/IPAC IRSA resources. The project runs on a standard laptop.

Our creative approach combines scientific processing with an accessible visual experience. We considered scientific reliability, image alignment, uncertainty, artifact warnings, accessibility, archive outages, performance, and presentation reliability. A precomputed offline edition ensures the demonstration remains available even without live data access.
